pages.quiz:
HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — MOCK EXAM #10
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which Sanskrit word means water? (1 mark)
   A. Vayu
   B. Jal
   C. Agni
   D. Prithvi

2. Where did Prince Siddhartha sit under the Bodhi tree? (1 mark)
   A. Amritsar
   B. Lumbini
   C. Bodh Gaya
   D. Nairobi

3. The Beas river is linked with which region of India? (1 mark)
   A. Bengal
   B. Punjab
   C. Gujarat
   D. Kerala

4. Which Enlightened Being is Jain? (1 mark)
   A. Narsimha
   B. Guru Ram Das
   C. Parshvanath
   D. Prahlad

5. What rescue is Parshvanath known for in a well-known story? (1 mark)
   A. A snake in a burning log
   B. A lost cow
   C. A wounded swan
   D. A drowning child

6. Who brought Siddhartha up after his mother died? (1 mark)
   A. His cousin Devadatta
   B. His aunt Mahaprajapati Gotami
   C. A king
   D. A teacher

7. Where is Lumbini today? (1 mark)
   A. In Nepal
   B. In Punjab
   C. In Uganda
   D. In Kenya

8. Which Tirthankar is the twenty-third of Jainism? (1 mark)
   A. Buddha
   B. Mahavir
   C. Guru Nanak
   D. Parshvanath

9. What does Aparigraha mean? (1 mark)
   A. Take everything
   B. Do not be greedy or hold too many things
   C. Talk a lot
   D. Always be angry

10. Which of these is one of the six directions in the Sigalovada Sutta? (1 mark)
   A. Teachers
   B. Strangers
   C. Kings
   D. Rivers

11. Who asked that Bharat be made king? (1 mark)
   A. Queen Kaikeyi
   B. Ganga
   C. Sita
   D. Mahaprajapati

12. In what language was the Ramayan first written? (1 mark)
   A. Sanskrit
   B. English
   C. Gurmukhi
   D. Kiswahili

13. Who went into the forest with Ram? (1 mark)
   A. Kaikeyi
   B. Sita and Lakshman
   C. Vishwamitra
   D. Bharat and Shatrughna

14. Who was Sigala? (1 mark)
   A. A Jain monk
   B. A young man taught by the Buddha
   C. A king of Ayodhya
   D. A Sikh Guru

15. Which is a main message of Jain scriptures? (1 mark)
   A. Practise pride
   B. Take revenge
   C. Be greedy
   D. Practise Ahimsa

16. In which script is Guru Granth Sahib Ji written? (1 mark)
   A. Swahili script
   B. Roman
   C. Arabic
   D. Gurmukhi

17. From which Veda does the Gayatri Mantra come? (1 mark)
   A. Rig Veda
   B. Atharva Veda only
   C. Dhammapada
   D. Ramayan

18. What is prasad? (1 mark)
   A. A garden
   B. A kind of shoe
   C. Blessed food shared after prayers
   D. A prayer book

19. What does the story of Guru Nanak and Bhai Lalo teach? (1 mark)
   A. Cheating pays
   B. Rich people are wrong
   C. Wealth is proof of goodness
   D. Honest earnings are best

20. What is a skit? (1 mark)
   A. A dance only
   B. A map
   C. A game with rules
   D. A short act showing a story

21. What should you do if you break something at school? (1 mark)
   A. Own up
   B. Blame another child
   C. Give it away
   D. Run away

22. How did the boy in the example story practise Asteya? (1 mark)
   A. He found the owner of the purse
   B. He hid the purse
   C. He sold the purse
   D. He kept the money

23. Why is integrity compared to a strong wall? (1 mark)
   A. Because it is heavy
   B. Because walls are white
   C. One weak brick can make it fall
   D. Because it is tall

24. Who should be allowed to board first? (1 mark)
   A. The loudest
   B. The strongest
   C. Children, elders and people with disabilities
   D. The fastest

25. What should you do if you find an item left on the vehicle? (1 mark)
   A. Give it away
   B. Give it to the driver or conductor
   C. Keep it
   D. Throw it away

26. How does the breath in happen in Kapaal Bhaati? (1 mark)
   A. By itself
   B. By hand
   C. By force
   D. By humming

27. In Sasankasana, where do your arms go at the end? (1 mark)
   A. Stretched forward on the floor
   B. In the air
   C. On your head
   D. Behind your back

28. How can children with special needs take part? (1 mark)
   A. In their own way, such as breathing slowly or seated poses
   B. They cannot join
   C. By leaving
   D. Only by watching

29. Which mistake is common about Madaraka Day? (1 mark)
   A. Thinking it is Independence Day
   B. Knowing the flag is raised
   C. Knowing it is 1 June
   D. Knowing it is for patriots

30. What is a rite or ritual? (1 mark)
   A. A special action done in a set way at a festival
   B. A kind of food
   C. A river
   D. A school subject

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Give three reasons why prayer is a principle of Dharma. (3 marks)

32. Explain the Sikh idea of Kirat Karni. (2 marks)

33. Describe how to pray well. (4 marks)

34. Name two grahas in the traditional calendar that are not planets in modern science. (2 marks)

35. Describe what the Panchang is. (2 marks)

36. Explain the Jain teaching called Asteya. (2 marks)

37. Compare the teachings of Parshvanath and Guru Ram Das Ji. (5 marks)

38. Write the Indian names for Thursday and Friday. (2 marks)

39. Give three benefits of yoga. (3 marks)

40. Name two sacred rivers mentioned in the lesson. (2 marks)

41. Match each being with a teaching: Narsimha, Parshvanath, Buddha, Guru Ram Das Ji. (4 marks)

42. Explain how the days of the week are related to the solar system. (3 marks)

43. Explain why respect for the holy books of other faiths is important in Kenya. (5 marks)

44. A shopper gives you Ksh 500 and you buy items for Ksh 320. Work out the change and say what to do if you are given Ksh 200 by mistake. (4 marks)

45. Write three signs of integrity at school. (3 marks)

46. Give the meaning of Maha Shivratri. (2 marks)

47. Why should we not pollute rivers? (2 marks)
pages.answers:
HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — MOCK EXAM #10 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — Jal
   Jal (also Apas) means water.

2. C — Bodh Gaya
   He became the Buddha at Bodh Gaya.

3. B — Punjab
   The Beas flows in Punjab, where Sikhism began.

4. C — Parshvanath
   Parshvanath is a Tirthankar of Jainism.

5. A — A snake in a burning log
   He asked the man to stop and the snake was saved.

6. B — His aunt Mahaprajapati Gotami
   His mother's sister looked after him.

7. A — In Nepal
   Lumbini lies in Nepal.

8. D — Parshvanath
   Parshvanath is the twenty-third Tirthankar.

9. B — Do not be greedy or hold too many things
   Aparigraha is non-greed.

10. A — Teachers
   Parents, teachers, family, friends, workers and holy teachers.

11. A — Queen Kaikeyi
   Kaikeyi reminded the king of two promises.

12. A — Sanskrit
   It was written in Sanskrit by Valmiki.

13. B — Sita and Lakshman
   Sita and Lakshman chose to go with him.

14. B — A young man taught by the Buddha
   The talk was given to him.

15. D — Practise Ahimsa
   Ahimsa is central in Jainism.

16. D — Gurmukhi
   It is written in Gurmukhi.

17. A — Rig Veda
   The Gayatri Mantra comes from the Rig Veda.

18. C — Blessed food shared after prayers
   Prasad is blessed food.

19. D — Honest earnings are best
   Honest work is valued.

20. D — A short act showing a story
   Skits help us learn lessons.

21. A — Own up
   Owning up shows integrity.

22. A — He found the owner of the purse
   He returned it.

23. C — One weak brick can make it fall
   Small lies can weaken trust.

24. C — Children, elders and people with disabilities
   We care for those who need help.

25. B — Give it to the driver or conductor
   Returning it shows integrity.

26. A — By itself
   It happens on its own.

27. A — Stretched forward on the floor
   Arms are stretched forward.

28. A — In their own way, such as breathing slowly or seated poses
   Everyone can take part.

29. A — Thinking it is Independence Day
   Independence is 12 December.

30. A — A special action done in a set way at a festival
   Examples are lighting a lamp or raising a flag.

SECTION B
----
31. (3 marks)
   Answer: It makes us thankful, calm and humble, gives courage, and reminds us we are not alone (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

32. (2 marks)
   Answer: Earning a living by honest work.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for earning and 1 mark for honest work.

33. (4 marks)
   Answer: Sit quietly, fold hands, think of God with love, say thanks, ask for wisdom and kindness, and end with a promise to do good (any four).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

34. (2 marks)
   Answer: The Sun and the Moon.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

35. (2 marks)
   Answer: The Indian traditional calendar book that lists days, months and festival dates.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for two points.

36. (2 marks)
   Answer: Not taking what is not given, or not stealing.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for a correct meaning.

37. (5 marks)
   Answer: Parshvanath taught Ahimsa, truth, not taking what is not given and not being greedy. Guru Ram Das Ji taught equality, honest work, humility and service. Both teach kindness and care for others.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for each teaching set and 1 mark for a comparison.

38. (2 marks)
   Answer: Thursday: Guruvaar. Friday: Shukravaar.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

39. (3 marks)
   Answer: It keeps the body flexible and strong, helps us breathe well and stay calm, helps us focus and teaches discipline (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

40. (2 marks)
   Answer: The Ganga and the Beas (or the Rijubalika).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct river.

41. (4 marks)
   Answer: Narsimha: God protects the good. Parshvanath: Ahimsa. Buddha: kindness to the hurt. Guru Ram Das Ji: honest work, equality and service.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct match.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: They are named after the Sun, the Moon and five planets that people could see in the sky, so each day has a heavenly partner.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for Sun and Moon, planets and naming.

43. (5 marks)
   Answer: Kenya has people of many faiths, and respect helps us live in peace and unity. Making fun of another's holy book hurts feelings and causes conflict. Listening and learning builds understanding.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for many faiths, 1 mark for peace and unity, 1 mark for hurt feelings, 1 mark for learning, 1 mark for a clear example.

44. (4 marks)
   Answer: Change is 500 minus 320 = Ksh 180. If given Ksh 200, that is Ksh 20 too much, so return the Ksh 20 to the shopkeeper.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 500 minus 320, 1 mark for 180, 1 mark for the extra 20, 1 mark for returning it.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: Not cheating, owning up to mistakes, handing in lost items, telling the truth, doing your own work (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: The great night of Lord Shiva.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for great night and 1 mark for Shiva.

47. (2 marks)
   Answer: Polluted rivers harm plants, animals and people who use the water, and take away the sacredness of the water.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid reason.
